title: Timbre: stochastic latency vs cost snapshot (sketch)
content:
Context and goal:
This is a working sketch for an internal one-pager comparing stochastic (traffic-driven) latency profiles against steady-state cost for three inference deployment shapes we care about: Hosted (multi-tenant fastpath), Dedicated A100 (reserved, high-IO), and Dedicated A100 quantized (int8-ish). The aim is to capture a small, portable narrative + ASCII charts we can drop into slides or product collateral after iteration.

Notes to self / assumptions (quick):
- Workload: conversational assistant, average prompt+response length 120 tokens, bursts follow a Poisson mix: 70% single-turn, 25% short multi-turn (2-4 turns), 5% long (5+ turns).
- Key metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms) for generation-only, and $/M tokens served (hosted list-price proxy).
- Using internal microbench numbers (see linked_artifacts). Quantized path trades off ~10% quality under long-turn regen but reduces per-token GPU time ~35%.
- Warm cache KV hit assumed: 40% for sessionized Dedicated, 10% for Hosted.

Executive sketch (one paragraph):
Timbre snapshot: for conversational workloads with intermittent bursts, Dedicated A100 yields the best p95/p99 tail under sustained concurrency but at a higher unit cost; quantization lowers cost per token substantially while increasing tail variance for long-turn sessions; Hosted multi-tenant is cheapest to start but shows p99 amplification during microbursts (short surges), which can be partially mitigated by session-aware prefetching. This doc enumerates the raw numbers we observed and an annotated ascii chart to make tradeoffs concrete.

Raw numbers (table of observed medians across three experimental runs):

Config | p50 (ms) | p95 (ms) | p99 (ms) | $ / M tokens (approx)
Hosted-fastpath  | 68   | 210  | 520  | $120
Dedicated-A100   | 45   | 110  | 210  | $310
Dedicated-A100-quant | 60  | 150  | 360 | $200

Interpretation bullets:
- p50: Dedicated-A100 best due to fewer context switch and pinning; quantization adds a small overhead for decode paths which slightly raises p50 vs fp16.
- p95/p99: Hosted amplifies tails under short bursts because multiplexing adds queuing; Dedicated has predictable tails but higher baseline $/M.
- Cost: quantized Dedicated gives ~35% cheaper tokens vs fp16 Dedicated, still ~60% more expensive than Hosted baseline in this pricing model.
- KV cache effect: when session KV hits rise from 10% -> 50%, Dedicated p50 improves ~8-12ms, Hosted improves ~4-6ms (absolute), but tail improvements concentrate on p95.

Small ASCII visual: p99 vs $/M scatter (rows are configs). Scale is symbolic to avoid hard plotting; higher X -> higher $; higher Y -> higher p99.

Key: $--- low ($) ; $++++ high ($) ; p99: | low (top) -> high (bottom)

Hosted-fastpath    : $---    | p99: ||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||||  (520ms)
Dedicated-A100     : $++++   | p99: |||||||||||||||| (210ms)
Dedicated-A100-q   : $++     | p99: |||||||||||||||||||||||| (360ms)

Burst profile vignette (text timeline):
- t0: idle -> single request arrives -> Hosted routes to fastpath, Dedicated wakes a warm slot.
- t0+120ms: more requests arrive (spike) -> Hosted queues on multiplexer -> p95 jumps; Dedicated uses session pinning -> p95 stable but consumes reserved concurrency.
- t0+800ms: spike decays -> Hosted draining leads to p99 spikes for a few seconds.

Developer-facing recommendations (draft):
- If customer SLO is p95 < 200ms and traffic is bursty, prefer Dedicated-A100 unless price sensitivity is dominant.
- If customer wants best $/M at low sustained volume, Hosted with aggressive prefetch + client-side pacing is viable but add p99 alarms.
- For mid-tier customers optimize for quantized Dedicated as sweet spot: saves ~35% token $ while maintaining p95 within 150ms for typical sessions.

Open questions / follow-ups (todo):
- Run the same sweep with H100 (we suspect ~20% p50 improvement on fp16 but need numbers).
- Measure quality regressions for quantized path on our long-turn regen prompt set (linked).
- Repeat benchmarks with 50% KV hit and 90% KV hit to better parametrize caching benefit.
- Add cost modelling for reserved vs burst-bucket pricing (monthly amortization).

Quick links / references (internal):
- Confluence: OPT-tiling-playbook (prefetch + tiling notes)
- Jira: OPT-4221 (quantization rollout tracking)
- Bench repo PR: github/bench/PR-87 (scripts + raw outputs)

Speaker notes / talking points (for briefing):
- "Quantization is our primary near-term lever to cut unit cost without changing routing policies. It's not free — expect higher tail risk on long sessions."
- "Hosted is great for small teams — but call out p99 risk explicitly in onboarding docs and enable prefetch toggles by default for chat endpoints."
- "Dedicated should be sold as predictable latency with optional quantization option for price-sensitive enterprise customers."

Rough checklist to convert to client-facing collateral:
- Pull high-resolution p99 traces from PR-87 and convert to small heatmap image (design ask).
- Draft 1-pager with two ascii charts replaced by proper visuals (product + sales review).
- Short side-bar on quality delta for quantized path (with links to eval scores).

Notes / stray thoughts (informal):
- Name "Timbre" because we want a short mnemonic for tail-shape vs price tradeoff. Might be useful internally when routing policies reference a profile.
- Keep this doc intentionally terse; will expand after H100 run.

-- Aisha (sketch)
